a: Attackers inject SQL via inputs; prevent with parameterized queries.
Stored XSS saves malicious script on the server and hits later visitors.
Reflected XSS echoes attacker input in a response immediately.
CSRF makes a logged-in browser perform unwanted actions; use tokens.
Clickjacking tricks users into clicking hidden UI via iframes.
../ sequences access unintended files; canonicalize and restrict paths.
Untrusted input passed to shells can run OS commands; avoid shells and escape.
Deserializing untrusted data can execute code or alter logic.
Default passwords, open admin panels, and verbose errors are common misconfigs.
Users access others' data/actions due to missing authorization checks.
